shipped.warum: Where the quarrel begins, from Palacký's Documenta (1869), read against the page images with a working translation: the king gives the Bohemian nation three votes at the university of Prague, the three other nations petition and swear to leave, and a Bohemian master defends the decree: 'the head and not the tail', and 'I am the truth, not the custom'.

shipped.kurz: Peter of Mladoňovice: the trial and death of Hus
shipped.warum: The eyewitness account of Hus's party, from Palacký's Documenta (1869), read against the page images with a working translation: Sigismund's safe conduct, the arrest of 28 November 1414, the king's words at the hearings of June 1415 ('do not believe him if he recants'), the sentence, the degradation and the burning of 6 July.

Six letters, from the arrival without safe conduct to the eve of the end, in the original Latin or Czech from Palacký (1869) with Workman and Pope's English (1904): the gaolers' flight, the king's word 'as little to be trusted as the safe-conduct', why he cannot abjure, 'God will raise up braver men', and 'Sigismund hath acted deceitfully throughout'.

shipped.kurz: The king's word and the council's (1415)
shipped.warum: From Palacký's Documenta, read against the page images with a working translation: Sigismund revokes every safe conduct he gave at Constance (8 April 1415); 250 lords write to him in Czech that Hus was 'seized under your safe conduct' and that no one will trust his safe conducts again (12 May); and the council explains to Bohemia why Hus was burned (26 July).

shipped.kurz: The council's decrees: Haec sancta and the sentence
shipped.warum: From Mansi's collection (1784), read against the page images with a working translation: Haec sancta, by which the council claimed its power immediately from Christ (6 April 1415); the sentence of 6 July 1415 against Hus as 'Wyclif's disciple' and 'a true and manifest heretic'; and five of the thirty condemned articles.

Five passages from the book the council drew its articles from, in David Schaff's English (1915), read against the page images: the Church of the predestined, Christ nearer than a pope two thousand miles away, the avaricious pope as 'the vicar of Judas', 'to rebel against an erring pope is to obey Christ', and 'no superior is above correction'.

shipped.kurz: Ulrich Richental's chronicle of the council
shipped.warum: The Constance citizen's German chronicle (Buck 1882), read against the page images with a working translation: Hus caught in a haycart, 'why have you broken your safe conduct yourself?', and the king handing the condemned man over 'in our stead'.

shipped.kurz: The protest of the Bohemian lords (2 September 1415)
shipped.warum: The letter of the lords of Bohemia and Moravia to the council under 452 seals, from Palacký's Documenta (1869), read against the page images with a working translation: Hus 'a good, just and catholic man', condemned unconfessed and unconvicted; whoever calls Bohemia heretical lies on his own head, King Sigismund excepted; and the preachers of the law of Christ to be defended 'even to the shedding of blood'.

shipped.kurz: Poggio on the trial of Jerome of Prague (1416)
shipped.warum: A humanist at the council writes to Leonardo Bruni, from Palacký's Documenta (1869), read against the page images with a working translation: Jerome's eloquence 'nearer to the ancients', 'bread remains at the baker's', the unjustly condemned from Socrates to 'a council of priests', the praise of Hus that sealed his fate, and 'a man worthy of everlasting memory'.

The Prague chronicler, from Fontes rerum Bohemicarum V (1893), read against the page images with a working translation: Mount Tábor and the defenestration of 30 July 1419, 'the common people and Jan Žižka', the king's death, the images broken and the Charterhouse burned, the war in Prague and the truce of November; Plzeň and the five cities, the shafts of Kutná Hora, the crusade proclaimed, Sudoměř behind the wagons, Prague's oath, Tábor's captains; the battle of Vítkov, the Four Articles of Prague, and Sigismund crowned in the castle and cursed by his own army as a 'patron and deceiver of heretics'.

missing.warum: The treatise is carried in David S. Schaff's English (1915). The only critical edition of the Latin, S. Harrison Thomson's (Boulder 1956), is in copyright, and the sixteenth-century printings are not available in usable scans. Where the council condemned a sentence from the book, the Latin article is carried in the council's decrees. A gap by necessity.
missing.quelle: Magistri Johannis Hus Tractatus de ecclesia, ed. S. H. Thomson (1956), in copyright.

missing.warum: The sermons, the Exposition of the Faith and the shorter Czech treatises are the Hus his Prague hearers knew. They are in the public domain in K. J. Erben's edition (1865–1868), but this stage follows the trial and its consequences, and carries Hus's Czech only in his letters. A gap by choice, and the first candidate for a later stage.
missing.quelle: Mistra Jana Husi Sebrané spisy české, ed. K. J. Erben, 3 vols. (Prague 1865–1868).

missing.kurz: Von der Hardt's acts of the council
missing.warum: Hermann von der Hardt's Magnum oecumenicum Constantiense concilium (1697–1700) is the fullest printing of the council's acts, and volume IV holds the sessions of 1415. No usable scan of that volume was found; the decrees are carried from Mansi XXVII (1784), which reprints the same acts.
missing.quelle: H. von der Hardt, Magnum oecumenicum Constantiense concilium, vol. IV (Frankfurt and Leipzig 1699).

missing.warum: Mladoňovice's account of Hus's death is carried, as the record of his last words. The other descriptions of the executions, Richental's of Hus and Poggio's of Jerome, and the chronicle pictures of the burnings, are not; the cuts are marked and the notes say what they contain. Laurence's accounts of crusaders burning Utraquist priests, peasants and children in 1420 are likewise left out. A gap by choice.

This apparatus ends with Sigismund's coronation and the crusade's retreat. The field armies, Žižka's military ordinance of 1423, the later crusades and Lipany (1434) are the subject of the companion site The Hussite Field Armies, which carries Laurence of Březová from 22 August 1420 on.
